speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative review. I see you experienced shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started relative to your surgery and if the pain is triggered by touching your ear or inserting anything into it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Tertiary Facial Nerve Paralysis.

The specific combination of shooting ear pain triggered by chewing and difficulty tolerating earrings 12 weeks post-tympanoplasty is classic for incomplete facial nerve regeneration affecting the stapedius and orbicularis oculi muscles. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelid or an inability to close your right eye completely?
